column2: Want to come to my room?”
I said, summoning my nerve.
“You're not thinking of anything weird at a time like this, are you?”
“Of course not!{r}{P}
I just...”
“I'll come, but
don't try anything funny.”
“Obviously not!{r}{P}”
It was unsettling to turn off the lights, so we left everything as it was and went upstairs.
As we climbed the stairs, Mr. Mikimoto suddenly swayed toward me.
“Are you all right?{r}{P}”
“Sorry.
I got a little dizzy...”
But he managed to reach his room on his own feet.
“Well...
be careful.”
With that last remark, Mr. Mikimoto went into his room.
I wasn't sure what I was supposed to be careful about, but it felt like a very fitting thing to say at this moment.
I opened the door to my room and let her in first.
I sat down beside her and put an arm around her shoulders.
{n2} stiffened for a moment but said nothing.
In a situation like this, I couldn't possibly feel like fooling around.
I pulled {n2} toward me and tried to kiss her.
“What are you doing?!{r}{P}”
Suddenly shoved away, I tumbled off the bed.
“At a time like this...
at a time like this!{r}{P}{p}I'm disappointed in you!{r}{P}”
{n2} was furious.
you don't have to be that angry...”
Before I could apologize, {n2} ran out of the room.
I hurried after her, but she slipped into her own room and
locked it from the inside.
I'm sorry.{r}{p}I won't do that again, so let's stay together.
Okay?{r}{P}”
I sounded like a cheating husband.
But no matter how many times I called, {n2} didn't even answer.
“Don't open the door for anyone.{r}{p}If anything happens, call out loudly.”
I called that out and went back to my room.
I regretted not considering the time and place, but it was too late.
If anything happened to {n2}...
I'd never forgive myself.
I sat down near the door and decided to listen for noises in the hallway.
At the slightest suspicious sound, I'd rush out to {n2}.
Time flowed slowly, and before I knew it I had fallen asleep...
I woke with a start and looked at the watch still on my wrist. It was 3:50.
Hoping nothing had happened, I decided to go check {n2}'s room again.
I thought of pounding on doors to call for help.
Without even checking whose doors they were, I ran down the hallway knocking on nearly every one.
“Excuse me!{r}{P}
Anyone! Wake up!{r}{P}”
...Only a suffocating silence.
As I was about to call out again, a horrible thought struck me.
What if...
what if everyone but me had already been killed?{r}{P}
And {n2} too...?
I froze.
I heard the stairs creaking behind me.
Someone was coming up to the second floor!
Instantly, I thought,
It had to be {n2}.
Is that you?{r}{P}”
I turned around boldly.
It was {n2}.
was alive!{r}{P}
Relief flooded my whole body.
She threw herself into my chest.
I held her trembling shoulders tightly.
“...What's wrong?
That scream earlier...
was that you?{r}{P}”
She seemed to nod.
“Uncle...
Uncle and Aunt...”
That was enough for me to guess roughly, but
I didn't want to admit it.
Had someone struck again, this time at the Kobayashis?{r}{P}
There was no way.
Innocent people being killed one after another,
that couldn't be allowed.
“No way...
Not even the Kobayashis...?{r}{P}”
In my arms, {n2} nodded repeatedly in silence as I asked in a daze.
“Who on earth...”
Murmuring that, I remembered Mr. Kayama in the cellar.
Might Mr. Kayama have gotten out of the cellar and killed the Kobayashis...?{r}{P}
I had to go check on the Kobayashis as soon as possible.
I took {n2}'s hand.
But when I tried to go downstairs, she shook her head and resisted.
I don't want to go back there.”
She must have seen something truly horrifying.
I couldn't bring myself to force her.
But I couldn't leave her here, either.
“You don't have to go inside, just come along with me.{r}{p}And I'll be right there with you!{r}{P}”
When I said it with conviction, she reluctantly agreed.
A mop handle lay on the floor.
I picked it up and held it ready.
Come to think of it, Mr. Kayama...
what had become of Mr. Kayama, locked in the cellar?{r}{P}
Could Mr. Kayama have gotten out of the cellar and killed the Kobayashis...?
From here, the cellar was closer.
Uneasy, I decided to check the cellar first.
The cellar door was open.
No way...
Rising dread pounded hard in my chest.
We hurried toward the Kobayashis' room.
At the end of the first-floor hallway were three rooms.
In front of the very last room, {n2} suddenly stopped.
The hand I'd been holding was tugged lightly.
“Is that where...?{r}{P}”
{n2} nodded.
I gulped, let go of {n2}'s hand, and stepped into the room.
I wanted to check on the Kobayashis.
When I took {n2}'s hand and tried to go further in, she shook her head and resisted.
I don't want to go back there.”
She must have seen something truly horrifying; I couldn't bring myself to force her.
But I couldn't leave her here, either.
“You don't have to go inside.{r}{p}And I'll be right there with you.”
When I said it with conviction, {n2} reluctantly agreed to come along.
I picked up the mop handle lying in the lounge and, holding it ready, went further in.
Had Mr. Kayama gotten out of the cellar and killed the Kobayashis, or...?
Going around the stairs and further on, there were three rooms.
In front of the very last room, {n2} suddenly stopped.
“In there...?{r}{P}”
{n2} nodded.
I gulped, let go of her hand, and stepped into the room.
The light was still on.
A cozy kitchen and the tatami living room beside it were brightly lit.
A perfectly ordinary family dining area.
Looking at it like this, nothing seemed out of the ordinary.
Mr. Kobayashi was there.
He sat on the floor with his back against the wall and his legs stretched out.
A kitchen knife was plunged into Mr. Kobayashi's belly, and the floor where he sat had become a sea of blood.
He must have tried to pull it out himself; both hands gripped the knife as if he'd committed seppuku.
Stomach acid rose and I covered my mouth with my hand.
I was about to be sick, so I rushed for the bathroom.
The moment I opened the bathroom door, something fell toward me.
A bloodstained hand.
“Gah!{r}{P}”
I cried out involuntarily.
The bathroom was covered in blood.
Kyoko, naked, was slumped against the bathtub.
Her vacant eyes, like glass beads, stared fixedly at me.
I knew at a glance that she was no longer breathing.
This was what had made {n2} scream.
To her, they were her blood relatives, her uncle and aunt.
It couldn't have been only fear.
How great a shock she must have suffered...
Thinking of {n2}'s feelings, I felt a painful, pitying ache I couldn't bear.
I hurried outside and found {n2} standing there, eyes brimming with tears.
So it's true...?{r}{P}”
She seemed to be asking if they were dead.
If I could, I'd have denied it for her, but...
I lowered my eyes and nodded.
“Huh?{r}{P}”
I felt as if a figure had passed across the far end of the passage.
“What is it?{r}{P}”
“No,
I thought someone was over there...”
I pointed, and suddenly went cold.
Had the killer been watching us?
Was it Mr. Kayama, or someone else...?{r}{P}
I couldn't tell anything anymore.
{n2} gripped my arm painfully hard.
I'm scared.”
“...It's okay.
Don't leave my side.”
I re-gripped the mop handle with my sweaty hand and slowly returned to the lounge.
I felt as if I could hear someone's breathing, and my heart pounded like an alarm bell.
I reached the cellar door.
It was open.
Wait.{r}{P}
Who had unlocked it?
“Mr. Kayama?{r}{P}”
I called toward the stairs leading down.
No answer.
I lowered my foot slowly and went down the stairs one step at a time.
The hand behind me still held {n2}'s hand firmly.
A bare bulb was the only light in the chilly wine cellar.
Under that light, Mr. Kayama lay face down.
His face was turned sideways, his eyes wide open.
A pool of dark blood a meter in radius had formed around his face.
Even Mr. Kayama...
I was no longer in a state to think straight.
A dismembered body, an unseen attacker, Midori beaten to death, and now the Kobayashis and Mr. Kayama...
This was no longer a situation for reasoning or solving puzzles.
How to survive until tomorrow morning.
Unless I thought about that, {n2} and I would be killed too.
I had no choice but to act on that thought.
“...I can't take it anymore...
I can't take it...!{r}{P}”
{n2} clung to me, turned her face from Mr. Kayama's body, and kept crying.
{n2}!{r}{P} Pull yourself together!{r}{P}{p} If you don't, we'll be killed too!{r}{P}”
I grabbed {n2}'s shoulders and shook her.
The light returned to her eyes, which had started to go vacant.
“Come on,
let's go back up.”
I didn't know what to do, but I didn't want to stay with the body any longer.
Watching our surroundings warily, we climbed the stairs.
I needed to call out to everyone and report the new incident.
And the first person I had to tell was Haruko.
Still holding {n2}'s hand, I went back to the second floor and knocked on everyone's door.
“Wake up!{r}{P}
Wake up!{r}{P} It's an emergency!{r}{P}
Please!{r}{P} Wake up!{r}{P}”
The first door to open a thin crack was the office girls' room.
Kanako was darting her eyes about, spotting {n2} and me.
She didn't seem to have changed clothes, so she must have been awake all along.
did something happen again?{r}{P}”
As I nodded gravely, Mr. Kayama's wife opened her door and came out into the hallway.
“Mrs. Kayama...
your husband...”
I faltered.
{n2} turned away, crying again.
Seeing us, she seemed to grasp the situation instantly.
The color drained from her face and Haruko staggered, steadying herself against the wall.
I rushed toward her, but she stopped me with a hand.
“...I'm all right,
I'm all right.{r}{p}Where is my husband?{r}{P}”
“In the cellar.
But for now I think it's better to stay together and not separate.”
I'd thought she might faint at hearing her husband was dead, but maybe she was much tougher than she looked.
“...That old man
...was killed?{r}{P}”
Kanako asked in a hushed voice.
“That's not all.{r}{p}It seems the Boss and his wife, too...”
“Th-
three people?!{r}{P}”
From behind her, I heard the other two gasp.
“Now that it's come to this, I think everyone should stay together.{r}{p}Could you let us...
or at least let Mrs. Kayama into your room?”
They seemed to confer in whispers inside for a while, then Kanako turned and nodded.
Haruko, her face blank as a doll's, went into the office girls' room as prompted.
There should be one more person on the second floor, Mr. Mikimoto.
Why hadn't he come out?{r}{P}
...Had he killed everyone?
“I'm going to check on Mr. Mikimoto.”
I told Kanako, and stood in front of Mr. Mikimoto's door.
I knocked with all my strength.
“Mr. Mikimoto!{r}{P}
Mr. Mikimoto! Aren't you there?{r}{P}”
Still no answer.
I quietly put my hand on the knob and turned it slowly.
Surprisingly, the door wasn't locked and opened easily.
Had he gone somewhere?
He hadn't.
Mr. Mikimoto was lying properly in bed.
What kind of nerve did it take not to lock the door in a situation like this?
Was he confident he wouldn't be killed, or was he himself...
I approached the bed and yelled in his ear.
“Mr. Mikimoto!{r}{P}
Wake up!{r}{P} Mr. Mikimoto!{r}{P}”
...But he didn't so much as twitch.
“Don't tell me...”
{n2} was speechless.
Could he be dead...
The same thought crossed my mind.
no way.{r}{p}He must just be tired.”
I timidly shook his body through the sheet.
“Mr. Mikimoto!{r}{P}
Mr. Mikimoto!{r}{P}”
He felt stiff as a log.
“Maybe...
check his pulse?{r}{P}”
“Don't say stupid things.{r}{p}He hasn't gotten hurt since then. Why would he die?”
Even as I said it, I quietly took hold of the arm lying outside the sheet.
It was ice cold, and I instinctively pulled my hand back.
“He's gone cold...”
Even Mr. Mikimoto was killed?{r}{P}
I hurriedly grasped his wrist again and carefully felt for a pulse.
so he's dead?{r}{P}”
{n2} asked, her face somewhere between crying and laughing.
All I could do was nod silently.
The pulse had stopped completely.
I stood there for a long while.
I couldn't think of anything.
Mr. Mikimoto, who would have been the most reliable if it came to confronting the killer.
Even he had been killed!
No, wait.
Had he really been killed?
“Maybe Mr. Mikimoto wasn't killed.”
When I said it, {n2} looked up in surprise.
“...What do you
...mean?{r}{P}”
“Mr. Mikimoto was hit hard on the head.{r}{p}Maybe back then he suffered a brain hemorrhage.{r}{p}If so, as time passed, blood would have collected inside his head and pressed on his brain
.{r}{p}If left untreated, he'd die.”
a natural death...?{r}{P}”
“The original cause was being hit, so
it's still murder in a sense, but...
since I can't find any other injury, I guess that's the only way to think about it.”
Either way, the fact that Mr. Mikimoto had died didn't change.
Still, it was easier to believe he'd died from his injury than to think a murderer had killed him.
Suddenly {n2} covered her mouth with her hand as if startled.
“What is it?{r}{P}”
“Mr. Mikimoto died here...{r}{p}Mr. Kayama, Uncle and Aunt too...{r}{p}Then the one who killed everyone must be...”
Only Toshio was left.
I realized it belatedly.
So the killer had been Toshio after all?{r}{P}
Had it all been an act, his grieving for Midori, his looking ready to kill Mr. Kayama?
“{n2}, let's go back!{r}{P}”
Grabbing {n2}'s hand, I dashed out of Mr. Mikimoto's room.
We went into Kanako's room, shut the door and locked it.
The three girls huddled in the corner of the room as if protecting themselves from us.
But they didn't seem to want to throw us out.
We'd better get out of this place.
It's no good anymore.{r}{p}Let's get out of here!{r}{P}”
“...Escape?
Do you have some way?{r}{P}{p}Are you going to abandon everyone else?{r}{P}”
{n2} looked back at me with cold eyes.
I was at a loss for an answer.
I'd said let's run on a whim, but going out into this blizzard was suicide.
And I couldn't stand being looked at like that by {n2}...
I steeled myself and began desperately thinking about what to do next.
I gulped and approached the door.
Careful not to touch the blood, I gripped the knob with my fingertips and turned it, but it was locked and wouldn't open.
So Toshio hadn't escaped from here...
Was that it?
Had he touched the knob by accident when passing through after killing the Kobayashis?{r}{P}
But the amount of blood on it seemed far too much for that.
It was as if he'd gripped the knob with a bloody hand.
That was the impression.
Worried about {n2}, I started running again.
I carefully undid the lock and pushed the door open a little.
The wind's roar grew louder and the blizzard blew in.
As I flinched for a moment, I saw something red in the snow.
Blood!{r}{P}
A large amount of blood had dripped onto the pure white snow, like shaved ice with garish strawberry syrup.
Whose...
blood was it?{r}{P}
Recovering from the shock, I wondered.
If Toshio had killed the Kobayashis, judging from the bodies he'd have been splattered to some degree.
But it couldn't flow like this.
Had someone else been killed again?{r}{P}
Or had Toshio himself been wounded by a desperate struggle while killing Mr. Kobayashi or someone?
I thought I should return to {n2} as fast as possible.
Thank goodness, we were saved.
I followed Kanako out, dashing down the stairs.
The chime kept ringing.
Kanako stood frozen before the entrance, frightened.
“What's wrong...?”
She didn't answer.
Outside, something fell with a thud.
Suspicious, I quietly went to the entryway and opened the inner door.
I had a bad feeling.
I approached the outer door and looked out through the glass.
Everything was white with the blizzard.
Looking down, I saw Toshio slumped against the door.
“Toshio...
Why was Toshio here?
Could it be a trap?{r}{P}
The thought flickered, but when I saw his face was covered in blood, I hurriedly opened the door.
The raging blizzard danced into the inn.
Toshio...
Unable to reach out, I murmured, looking down at him.
A faint voice reached me.
He's still alive!{r}{P}
Shaking off the suspicion of a trap, I put my ear close to Toshio's face.
“What happened?!{r}{P}
What on earth happened?{r}{P}”
Toshio gazed at my face with vacant eyes, and seemed to smile faintly.
Then in the next moment, with his eyes wide open, his head dropped limply to the side.
...He was dead.{g}
Toshio, who was supposed to be the killer, had died.
But why?
I heard someone crying.
Kanako.
Kanako had collapsed in the hall, sobbing.
I got up unsteadily, went inside, and firmly
shut both doors.
Only we were left alive.
We had all been in the same room.
Then who had killed Toshio?{r}{P}
And...
had Toshio really been the killer?
I thought that while I went to rescue her, Toshio might come into this room.
I turned and bit my lip, looking at {n2} and the others.
don't leave her alone!{r}{P}”
“But...
if Toshio comes this way...
“Don't worry about us.{r}{p}There are plenty of us, we'll be fine.{r}{p}More importantly, hurry and bring Kanako back.”
“...Okay.
Lock it as soon as I'm out.”
I grabbed the mop and dashed into the hallway.
